messages:
eva: Heads-up — PR gate failing for gha eval matrix.

eva: Steps to repro: open any PR, GH Actions starts, some matrix jobs never get a runner; others pick up multiple jobs. Seems tied to token rotation window we rolled yesterday.

eva: Error in runner logs: `registration failed: labels mismatch (expected: self-hosted,linux,x86,eval-runner) got: self-hosted,linux,x86,eval-runner,stale-token`

```
2024-11-12T09:21:03Z runner: received registration
2024-11-12T09:21:03Z runner: labels: [self-hosted linux x86 eval-runner stale-token]
2024-11-12T09:21:03Z runner: claimed by job 1234
2024-11-12T09:21:03Z job 1234: started but runner label check failed for matrix=quant-smoke
```

aaron: ugh. we saw a similar thing but for heartbeat tags last month. sounds like label metadata isn't being cleared when token swaps.

maddie: Is this just affecting PR gating or nightly too? Could be matrix size sensitive (we run 12 forks) :thinking_face:

eva: PR gating primarily. Nightly uses dedicated pool and seems fine. The problem is self-hosted runners are re-registering with an extra label `stale-token` while the GH Actions controller still expects the previous token->label combo, so job routing is inconsistent.

liam: Quick check: are we still using long-lived runner tokens for the autoscaler? We intended ephemeral tokens via the registration API.

ana: We switched to ephemeral in Oct but the autoscaler has a fallback path that reuses cached token if request fails. That cache TTL is 30m. If rotation happens during TTL expiry, label merge can happen.

maddie: Any easy mitigation to unblock PRs now?

eva: Temporary patch deployed to the autoscaler: purge cached token on rotation event. Should stop new runners from picking up `stale-token` label. But existing runners keep the label until re-register.

ci-bot: Deploy started: infra/autoscaler@v2.3.1 -> canary -> 3 nodes

aaron: Could we also relax the matrix label check to accept either label while we drain old runners? e.g., matrix -> accept `eval-runner` OR `eval-runner,stale-token` ?

liam: I'd rather avoid loosening gating. Alternative: schedule a rolling restart of self-hosted runners to force re-register with correct labels.

ana: Rolling restart would take ~25 minutes and will delay some PRs but is safest for correctness.

maddie: I'd propose: 1) purge cache (done), 2) start rolling restart of runners in batches of 10% with 2-min gap, 3) monitor gate failures and unpause canary after 10m if stable.

eva: +1. I'll start batch-1 now. tagging @eng-infra for coordination.

liam: Also let's add a short-term GH Action step that asserts runner labels before claiming job to produce clearer logs.

eva: Created PR to gha workflows with preflight check step. Link: https://github.com/redwood-inference/actions/compare/preflight-label-check

ana: Postmortem action items: 
- fix autoscaler token cache invalidation (PR done)
- add instrumentation to runner registration to emit label diffs
- make token rotation event emit a webhook to orchestration

aaron: Assigning owners: autoscaler cache fix -> @ana, rolling restart -> @eva, preflight workflow patch -> @liam

maddie: Monitoring: I'll watch PR gating channel and set a PagerDuty alert if >3 failures in 5m.

eva: Batch-1 done, 10% restarted, initial gate runs look green.

ci-bot: Noted: 4 jobs failed with `labels mismatch` in last 10m (now decreasing).

eva: Will continue batches. If anyone sees odd job claim patterns DM me.

liam: After this stabilizes we should add an integration test in our eval harness CI to simulate token rotation and verify runner label reconciliation.

eva: Agreed. I'll add a ticket to the eval-harness backlog.

maddie: thanks team :thumbsup:
